thread:
Aida (Manager): Heads-up: Marco asked to take Dec 26 off for a family holiday. That's inside the Dec 20-27 blackout. Can we get guidance on approvals and whether unpaid is OK?

Marco (IC): Sorry for the late ping. My partner's parents are only in town that weekend. I have 8 hours accrued but need 16. Happy to swap oncall or take unpaid for remaining.

PeopleOps Bot: Reminder: blackout days Dec 20-27 require manager approval + People Ops sign-off. Exceptions are allowed for compelling reasons with a coverage plan.

Nina (People Ops): Hi Aida/Marco. We do allow exceptions but prefer swaps/coverage. Process: submit TimeOff request with "Blackout Exception", attach manager attestation and coverage plan. If accruals are insufficient, you can select unpaid for the shortfall and mark it as "Unpaid Exception" so payroll handles it correctly.

Aida (Manager): I can cover the Monday morning sync and will swap Marco's non-prod duty with Priya. Coverage plan: Priya covers 09:00-12:00 on 26th, Aida covers PM triage. No oncall conflicts.

Marco (IC): Thanks Aida. I'll mark request as 8 hours PTO + 8 hours unpaid exception. Any concerns on audit?

Payroll Bot: Note for payroll: unpaid exceptions must be flagged in TimeOff ID. Also, accruals are consumed first; carryover will be used automatically if available.

Nina (People Ops): That's fine. Aida, please confirm manager attestation when Marco files. We aim to respond within 48 hours but will fast-track simple coverage cases.

Aida (Manager): Confirmed. Attestation: "I attest coverage is arranged as described; approving blackout exception for Marco."

Marco (IC): Submitted request ID 20300177 with manager attestation and coverage notes.

PeopleOps Bot: Request 20300177 queued for review.

Nina (People Ops): Approved. Marked as "Blackout Exception Approved: coverage verified". Policy ref PTO-3.2. I'll add a short audit note.

Marco (IC): Thanks all. I'll follow up on calendar updates.
